Hi team — quick answers + what I can share publicly: 

SOC 2:
- Redwood maintains a current SOC 2 Type II attestation (CC) covering security and availability. We can share the attestation under NDA — attached the latest PDF for initial review.

Deletion SLA (primary data):
- Standard offering: 30 calendar days from a verified customer deletion request (measured from request acknowledgement).
- Enterprise/BAA customers: we can offer accelerated deletion SLAs (down to 7 calendar days) for specific data classes (e.g., PHI) as a contractual commitment. This requires a product/ops change request and acceptance in contract (i.e., Dedicated or Private deployments typically).

Backups & secure purge:
- Default backup retention: 180 days. Backups are immutable for the retention window to ensure integrity.
- Secure purge of backups is possible but operationally involved: for enterprise customers we can initiate a targeted purge workflow that results in backups containing the deleted data being removed within a contractual window — target: 30–90 days depending on storage medium and cross-region replication. We can scope faster purge for Dedicated/Private.

Logs:
- Default logs retention: 365 days (used for troubleshooting and security investigations). Shorter retention windows can be offered under contract.

Measurement & verification:
- Deletion SLA measured from customer deletion request acknowledgement timestamp.
- We provide deletion confirmation receipts and can include audit logs for deletion events in an agreed format.

Attachments I can share now (subject to NDA): SOC2_Attestation.pdf, a filled copy of Redwood_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (I will pre-fill infra/security sections), and a Data_Processing_Addendum template for legal to review.

Suggested next step: Schedule a 30-min technical call (Neha + Marissa + Alex) to walk through backup purge mechanics and agree a timeline for the DPA/BAA.

Thanks — Neha Kapoor
